A Mini-Exodus Unfolds at Blackstone’s Marquee Real Estate Team
 
Plus, Boise’s rent rebound shows a splintering apartment market
 
By Craig Karmin
 

This is an edition of the Real Estate newsletter, a weekly briefing of the biggest commercial deals, news, analysis and trends in office, multifamily, retail and other commercial sectors. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 

Nearly a third of the unit’s senior managing directors have left the firm over the past three years, as its investment funds for the sector have slumped. Each of the dozen Blackstone real-estate executives departed for a variety of reasons. But a common thread runs through the mini-exodus: They were no longer making the money they had during their best years because Blackstone’s real-estate funds aren’t earning as much. “Many top dealmakers feel their professional opportunity has plateaued,” said Darin White Eydenberg, founder of Highridge Search. Peter Grant reports on why lower compensation tied to reduced profit is shaking up the investment business.

 

Boise’s rental housing market is back. Rents in the Idaho capital have risen more than 8% compared with last year, nearly the fastest in the U.S., while new supply is absorbed and the city rides the AI wave. Boise’s rent rebound illustrates how the national apartment market is splintering following this decade’s most significant boom-bust cycle. Rebecca Picciotto explains why other once-hot markets, such as Austin, Phoenix and Nashville, are still grappling with a glut of new apartments from years of overbuilding while Boise rentals thrive.

 
 
 

Dwindling Pay Fuels High-Profile Exits From Blackstone’s Marquee Real Estate Team

 
 
VICTOR J. BLUE/BLOOMBERG NEWS
 

A string of high-level departures from Blackstone’s real-estate business is shaking up the world’s biggest property investor. Nearly a third of the unit’s senior managing directors have left the firm over the past three years as its investment funds for the sector have slumped.

 

Nadeem Meghji, global head of real estate, shocked the firm in September when he said he was departing to spend more time with his family. His former co-head, Kathleen McCarthy Baldwin, left last year after 15 years with the firm.

How Boise Became One of America’s Hottest Rental Markets

 
 
 
 

Boise is in the third phase of a nationwide real-estate transformation that has defined this decade’s topsy-turvy housing market. After a pandemic-era housing boom followed by a sharp correction, the city is booming again, but this time only for rental housing.

 

Rents have risen more than 8% compared with last year, nearly the fastest in the U.S. Boise’s rebound illustrates how the national apartment market is splintering following this decade’s most significant boom-bust cycle.

 
 
 

Data Points

 

• $257 billion: The increase in mortgage balances on consumer credit reports in the third quarter, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Balances on home equity lines of credit jumped by $23 billion, the largest rise since 2005.

 

• $181,000: The annual household income needed to buy a median-priced home in a lower-priced neighborhood in the Greater Boston area, according to the latest Greater Boston Housing Report Card. That is up from $124,000 in 2021.

 

• 9.4 million: The square feet of industrial space leased in East-Southeast Far, Houston’s largest logistics market, during the first 10 months of the year, according to CoStar. That puts the market on pace for one of its strongest leasing years on record, though it is still working through a large industrial real-estate glut.
